facts.title: near hit - thermal exposure at P-4105

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was no injury or loss. The potential outcome was rated 2 against the site's consequence scale, above the 0 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control LOAD_SUPPORT_FOR_MAINTENANCE: the mechanical support of a load during maintenance access was in place but did not perform, and the accident investigation classified this as an absent or failed defence.
Control STORED_ENERGY_DISSIPATION: the dissipation or restraint of trapped and residual energy was not in place, and the accident investigation classified this as a task or environmental condition.
Control ZERO_ENERGY_VERIFICATION: the proving zero energy before intrusive work had been bypassed, and the accident investigation classified this as an absent or failed defence.

recommendations: Restore the mechanical support of a load during maintenance access on P-4105 and M-4105 and record the spot check before this task is next authorised.
Restore the proving zero energy before intrusive work on P-4105 and M-4105 and record the spot check before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in applying and verifying an isolation, specifically applying locks, tags and personal danger tags. P-4105 (hydrocarbon transfer pumps) is in service for hydrocarbon transfer, single mechanical seal with pressurised barrier-fluid support. The task proceeded during a breakdown response while the mechanical support of a load during maintenance access was in place but did not perform. The thermal energy involved is held as hot surface, and the recorded presentation was burn, ignition, scald.
response.summary: On 30 April 2006 a near hit was recorded on P-4105 and M-4105 at Marrindal Concentrator and Hydrocarbon Transfer Facility during a breakdown response; thermal energy held as hot surface was not released.
